'''Ioana Dumitriu''' (born July 6, 1976) is a Romanian-American mathematician who works as a professor of mathematics at the [[University of California, San Diego]].<ref name="cv">[http://www.math.washington.edu/~dumitriu/cv_2009.pdf Curriculum vitae], 2009, retrieved 2014-12-24. {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130925230318/http://www.math.washington.edu/~dumitriu/cv_2009.pdf |date=2013-09-25 }}</ref> Her research interests include the theory of [[random matrix|random matrices]], [[numerical analysis]], [[scientific computing]], and [[game theory]].

==Life==
Dumitriu is the daughter of two Romanian electrical engineering professors from [[Bucharest]]. Early in her life she was identified as having mathematical talent, and at age 11 won a national mathematics contest. She entered mathematics training camps in preparation for participation on the Romanian team at the [[International Mathematical Olympiad]], although her highest level of participation in the olympiad was the national semifinal.<ref name="nyt"/>
 
As a 19-year-old freshman at [[New York University]] (NYU), Dumitriu already was taking graduate-level classes in mathematics.<ref name="schafer"/> She graduated ''[[summa cum laude]]'' from NYU in 1999 with a B.A. in mathematics and a minor in computer science.<ref name="cv"/> She earned her Ph.D. in 2003 from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] under the supervision of [[Alan Edelman]], with a thesis on ''Eigenvalue statistics for beta-ensembles''.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=76759}}</ref><ref name="thesis">{{cite thesis|first=Ioana|last=Dumitriu|title=Eigenvalue statistics for beta-ensembles|date=2003|publisher=[[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]]|mr=2717094}}</ref> After postdoctoral research as a [[Miller Research Fellows|Miller Research Fellow]] at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], she joined the faculty of the [[University of Washington]] in 2006, moving to UC San Diego in 2019.<ref name="profile-ucsd">{{cite web|url=https://math.ucsd.edu/people/profiles/ioana-dumitriu/|title=Profile of Ioana Dumitriu|website=Department of Mathematics, University of California, San Diego}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
Dumitriu won the [[Alice T. Schafer]] prize for excellence in mathematics by an undergraduate woman in 1996.<ref name="schafer">[http://www.awm-math.org/schaferprize/1996.html Seventh Annual Alice T. Schafer Prize] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160730211511/http://www.awm-math.org/schaferprize/1996.html |date=2016-07-30 }}, [[Association for Women in Mathematics]], retrieved 2014-12-30.</ref> Also in 1996, as a sophomore at New York University, Dumitriu became the first woman to become a Putnam Fellow, meaning that she earned one of the top five scores at the [[William Lowell Putnam Mathematical Competition]].<ref name="nyt">{{citation|title=Q: How Many Women Have Won the Top Math Contest?|newspaper=[[New York Times]]|first=Karen W.|last=Arenson|date=May 1, 1997|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1997/05/01/nyregion/q-how-many-women-have-won-the-top-math-contest.html}}</ref> In 1995, 1996, and 1997 she won the Elizabeth Lowell Putnam Award that is given to the top woman in the contest, a record that was not matched until ten years later when [[Alison Miller]] also won the same award in three consecutive years.<ref>[http://www.maa.org/news/putnam-competition-results-harvard-captures-top-prize Putnam Competition Results: Harvard Captures Top Prize], [[Mathematical Association of America]], March 17, 2008, retrieved 2014-12-24.</ref>

She won the [[Leslie Fox Prize for Numerical Analysis]] (given to a young [[numerical analysis]] researcher who excels both mathematically and in presentation skills) in 2007.<ref>[http://www.ima.org.uk/about_us/awards_and_medals/ima_leslie_fox_prize/previous_winners.html IMA Leslie Fox Prize for Numerical Analysis Winners], retrieved 2014-12-24.</ref> In 2009 she received a [[National Science Foundation CAREER Awards|CAREER Award]] from the [[National Science Foundation]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=0847661|title=CAREER Award|website=nsf.gov|access-date= 2018-03-24}}</ref> In 2012, she became one of the inaugural [[fellow]]s of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2014-12-24.</ref>
